name: system-vitals
description: CPU, GPU, memory, disk and battery monitoring in the VS Code status bar, with native Apple Silicon GPU support.

systemvitals.show.cpuusage.description: Toggles the display of CPU Usage.

systemvitals.show.cpufreq.description: Toggles the display of CPU frequency. For Windows, this displays the maximum clock speed.

systemvitals.show.mem.description: Toggles the display of memory consumption.

systemvitals.show.battery.description: Toggles the display of battery percentage remaining if a device with a battery. If the device reports not having a battery, this setting will always be treated as false.

systemvitals.show.disk.description: Toggles the display of disk space information.

systemvitals.show.cputemp.description: Toggles the display of CPU temperature. May not work without the lm-sensors module on Linux. May require running VS Code as admin on Windows

systemvitals.show.gpu.description: Toggles the display of GPU utilization. macOS only; automatically hidden on machines that do not report GPU statistics.

systemvitals.show.gpumem.description: Toggles the display of GPU memory in use. macOS only; automatically hidden on machines that do not report GPU statistics.

systemvitals.gpu.sampleintervalms.description: How often, in ms, GPU utilization is read while the GPU is busy. macOS reports utilization as a span between reads rather than as a level, so readings taken far apart run high: lowering this makes the percentage more accurate and costs more CPU, raising it does the reverse. Each read costs roughly 28ms of CPU, so the 250ms default spends around 10% of one core while the GPU is working. Polling relaxes to every 2s once the GPU goes idle, which costs about 2% of a core, and stops entirely when the reading is hidden. Slower than about 500ms reports 87-96% for a load that is truly 47%, which is no better than not averaging at all.

systemvitals.disk.format.description: Configures how the disk space is displayed (percentage remaining/used, absolute remaining, used out of totel).

systemvitals.disk.drives.description: Drives to show. For example, 'C:' on Windows, and '/dev/sda1' on Linux.

systemvitals.updatefrequencyms.description: How long in ms between updates to resources. This governs the hover details as well as the status bar, so the two always agree. VS Code redraws an open hover whenever its content changes, so short intervals make the details flicker while you are reading them.

systemvitals.show.precision.description: Number of decimal places shown for each resource.

systemvitals.alignLeft.description: Toggles the alignment of the status bar.

systemvitals.color.description: Color of the status bar text in hex code (for example, #FFFFFF is white). The color must be in the format #RRGGBB, using hex digits.
